subject: Deployment pathway and concurrency follow-up (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: David Li <david.li@quantifai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment pathway and concurrency follow-up (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

David — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups to help us size a Dedicated proposal (if you choose reserved capacity) or guide Hosted/Private tradeoffs: 

Summary from the call:
- Primary use: inference for real-time scoring + light batch re-ranking.
- Target p95 latency goal: ~200ms for short requests (we flagged this as soft).
- Current traffic shape: expected 350 avg reqs/min (6 RPS) rising to 1,200 reqs/min peak (20 RPS) during events.
- Token mix: short prompts (~150 tokens) + average completion ~220 tokens; 95th percentile sequences can be ~2,000 tokens for diagnostics.
- Data residency: US-only; eventual interest in VPC/private deployment for regulated customers.

Because the conversation touched on multiple deployment modes, here are specific clarifying asks so we can produce a concrete Dedicated SKU recommendation and a Hosted fallback plan: 

Action items / clarifying questions for you: 
1) Please confirm target steady-state TPS (requests per second) and peak TPS (we used 6 RPS steady, 20 RPS peak in the notes above).
2) P50/P95 latency SLO you want us to guarantee for dedicated (e.g., P95 < 250ms).
3) How much batching can you tolerate? Are requests highly independent or can you accept small batch windows (10-30ms) to improve throughput?
4) Can you share a small sample of anonymized tokenized payloads (prompt/completion distributions)? I attached a capacity worksheet — filling the token buckets there will let us run a sizing calc.
5) Any hard constraints (no GPUs above X cost, or must be multi-region)?

Provisional sizing notes (very preliminary):
- If you want predictable reserved throughput and low P95 for 300–500 RPS-equivalent tokens (based on your token mix), H100s give better headroom for high-concurrency real-time use cases; A100s can be more cost-efficient for steady, medium-throughput workloads when using batching and quantization.
- For your stated average/peak, a 2x H100 reserved pool with autoscale burst to 4x for peak events is a reasonable starting point, pending precise token distribution.

I attached a quick capacity worksheet and a one-page deployment matrix. Fill the worksheet fields you can and we’ll convert to explicit GPU counts, expected token/sec, estimated monthly cost for Dedicated, and a Hosted fallback profile.

Next step: if you can answer the 5 items above, I’ll circulate a draft SOW + a comparison table (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). Want to schedule a 30-min ops deep-dive next week to finalize concurrency and region choices?

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
attachments: capacity_worksheet_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), deployment_matrix_summary.pdf (pdf)

From: David Li <david.li@quantifai.com>

Subject: Re: Deployment pathway and concurrency follow-up (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Alex — thanks for the writeup, helpful. Couple quick answers and a few more specific asks so we can move to a sizing decision: 

Answers: 
- Confirming our estimated steady/peak: steady ~8 RPS (480 rpm), peak ~28 RPS (1680 rpm) for the next quarter as we onboard two large customers.
- Desired SLO: P95 end-to-end latency < 300ms for the real-time scorer.
- Batching tolerance: We prefer minimal batching for inference because a lot of requests are user-facing; 5–10ms micro-batching is ok if it doesn’t push p95 above the SLO.
- Token distribution: your numbers are close — median prompt 130 tokens, median completion ~180 tokens. We do have a long-tail: 2–3% of requests hit ~1,500–2,500 tokens.
- Cost constraint: we’re sensitive to committed monthly cost; we’d rather trade a bit of latency for cost savings if the customer experience is not impacted.

Specific asks: 
1) Can you give concrete example SKU options with estimated throughput numbers (e.g., 1x H100 = X RPS at given token mix and P95 < 300ms)?
2) What concurrency per-GPU should we expect (requests that stay in KV cache vs cold starts)?
3) For private/VPC deployment later, what changes in SKU recommendations? Are there vendor-limited GPUs (e.g., L40S) that make sense for on-prem?

Also please indicate runbook for autoscale — how much buffer do you recommend?

If you can send a short table with 2–3 SKU scenarios (cost/throughput/latency) that maps to Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, we can share with our engineering leadership.

—David
David Li
CTO, Quantifai
david.li@quantifai.com

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: David Li <david.li@quantifai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 16:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment pathway and concurrency follow-up (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Thanks David — below is a concise SKU-level table and follow-ups. I kept the numbers conservative for P95 < 300ms with a 5–10ms micro-batch window. These are estimates; final numbers will come after you drop a sample event set into the attached worksheet.

SKU scenarios (rough estimates for your token mix: prompt 130 / completion 180 tokens):

1) Cost-conscious Dedicated (balanced) — A100 80GB flavor
- Typical: 1x A100 handles ~12–15 RPS steady with P95 ~220–300ms (depends on batch window).
- Concurrency: expect ~40–60 concurrent short requests per GPU before P95 degradation if batching is limited.
- Use case: steady workloads with batching and quantization enabled.

2) Low-latency Dedicated (headroom) — H100 80GB flavor
- Typical: 1x H100 handles ~20–30 RPS steady with P95 < 250ms with 5–10ms micro-batching.
- Concurrency: ~80–120 concurrent short requests per GPU with KV cache reuse.
- Use case: interactive scoring where p95 matters and peak surges occur.

3) Private / On-prem (cost & OEM availability) — L40S / L4x? (vendor dependent)
- Typical: L40S can be cost-effective for lower throughput; expect 1x L40S ~8–12 RPS for medium sequences.
- Caveat: on-prem performance varies by driver/kernel; we’ll need a brief ramp to validate.

Autoscale/runbook guidance:
- Buffer: reserve ~30% headroom on top of expected peak for autoscale decisions; schedule scale-up thresholds at 65–70% utilization and scale down after a 10–15 minute cool-off.
- Canary/fallback: keep a small Hosted pool as a fallback route for short-duration spikes or when Dedicated preemption occurs.

Questions for your engineers (to make the final worksheet run):
- Can you export a 24-hour sample of tokenized requests (timestamps + token counts) for us? Even 1–2k requests is enough for a sizing Monte Carlo.
- Any SLA language we should anticipate (penalties, RTO, RPO)?

Next steps:
- If you confirm we should prepare a formal Dedicated proposal, Marissa will run the capacity worksheet and produce a 3-option SKU quote (A100 baseline / H100 performance / hybrid A100+H100).
- Proposed calendar: ops deep-dive Wed 5/19 10:30am PT — will loop in infra/ops.

I’m attaching a draft SOW + the worksheet. I’ll also include expected monthly cost ranges once we have the tokenized sample.

Best,
Alex
